## Background

Today we are going to learn all about the **ggplot2** package in R.

There are tones of graphics packages in R. These include "base R graphics" (like the `plot()` function we used last day) and ad on packages like **ggplot2**.

### Comparing base graphics with ggplot

We can use the in-build data frame `cars` to play with plotting:

```{r}
head(cars)
```

```{r}
plot(cars)
```

Now with the ggplot:
First we need to install the package with `install.packages()`.

> I do not want to run `install.packages("ggplot2")` in my quarto document as this will result me reinstalling the package everytime when I render my report. -- just run the code in the console.

Every time I want to use a function from a given package I need to load up with a `library()` call:

```{r}
library(ggplot2)
ggplot(cars)
```

Every ggplot needs at least 3 things.

- the **data** (data.frame we want to plot from)
- the **aes** (how colums of the data map to the plot)
- the **geom** (how you want the plot drawn, points, lines, etc.)

```{r}
ggplot(data=cars) +
  aes(x=speed, y=dist) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method="lm") +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(x="Speed (MPH)",
       y="Stopping Distance (ft)",
       title= "Sily Plot of Stopping Distances")
```


## Gene Expression Plot

Read the data from outline:
```{r}
url <- "https://bioboot.github.io/bimm143_S20/class-material/up_down_expression.txt"
genes <- read.delim(url)
head(genes)
```


```{r}
ggplot(data=genes) +
  aes(x=Condition1, y=Condition2) +
  geom_point() +
  labs(x= "Control",
       y= "Drug")
```

> Q: How many gnes are in this dataset?

```{r}
nrow(genes)
```


> Q: How many are "up" regulated?

```{r}
sum(genes$State == "up")

```

```{r}
table(genes$State)
```

> Q: What perdentage of genes are "down" regulated?

```{r}
sum(genes$State=="down")
nrow(genes)
downgene <- sum(genes$State=="down")
totalgenes <- nrow(genes)
ans <- round(downgene/totalgenes*100, 4)
ans
```

The percentage of down genes is `r ans`% and that is that...

```{r}
myplot <- ggplot(genes) +
  aes(x=Condition1, y=Condition2, col=State) +
  geom_point() +
  scale_colour_manual(values=c("blue", "gray", "red")) +
  labs(x= "Control",
       y= "Drug Treatment",
       title = "Just Another Scater Plot Made with ggplot",
       subtitle = "GLP-1 inhibitor from Novo")
```

```{r}
myplot + theme_classic()
```

We can instal extra packages with `install.packages()` like theme packages for spongebob colors or actually useful ones line **patchwork** for combining plots:

```{r}
library(patchwork)
p1 <- ggplot(mtcars) + geom_point(aes(mpg, disp))
p2 <- ggplot(mtcars) + geom_boxplot(aes(gear, disp, group = gear))
p3 <- ggplot(mtcars) + geom_smooth(aes(disp, qsec))
p4 <- ggplot(mtcars) + geom_bar(aes(carb))

# Use patchwork to combine them here:
(p1 | p2) / 
(p3 | p4)
```


```{r}
p1 / (p2|p3|p4)
```

> Looking at parts of the data/doing multi-pannels. Separating the whole graph.

```{r}
myplot +
  facet_wrap(~State)
```

## The GapMinder Data

The gapminder dataset is rather famous and has lot of stuff we can plot.

```{r}
# File location online
url <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jennybc/gapminder/master/inst/extdata/gapminder.tsv"

gapminder <- read.delim(url)
```

Have a wee peak:
```{r}
head(gapminder)
```

> Q: How many data entries are there in this dataset?

```{r}
nrow(gapminder)
```

> Q: How many countries  in this dataset?

```{r}
countries <- unique(gapminder$country)
length(countries)
```

```{r}
myplot <- ggplot(gapminder) +
  aes(gdpPercap, lifeExp, col=continent) +
  geom_point(alpha=0.4)
myplot


```

add some color...
```{r}
myplot + facet_wrap(~continent)
```

```{r}
ggplot(gapminder) +
  aes(lifeExp, fill=continent)+
  geom_histogram()
```

```{r}
ggplot(gapminder) +
  aes(lifeExp, continent, fill=continent)+
  geom_boxplot()
```
